userStories.title: Build deterministic repo analysis for setup
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build the deterministic analysis layer that discovers repo shape, packages, package facts, and command availability for `nax setup`.

**Motivation** — The result is configs that reference commands the repo does not have.

**Approach** — Detection is **deterministic** (reuses existing detectors); command-mapping is **LLM-driven** (not regex/AST). The deterministic pass builds a `RepoAnalysis` fact object; the agent receives those facts and proposes the config.

**Scope** — In: `RepoAnalysis` / `PackageFacts` types, root-vs-package shape detection, package discovery, script inventory, missing-script detection, project profile detection, test-file-pattern detection, package-relative path normalization, package manager/orchestrator facts. Out: any LLM call path, config writing, verification, or script mutation.

**Interface**
```typescript
// Creates (per story)
// - src/cli/setup-analyze.ts
// - src/cli/setup-types.ts
```

**Notes** — Reuse detectors (do not duplicate): `detectStack()` (`src/cli/init-detect.ts`), `discoverWorkspacePackages()` (`src/test-runners/detect/workspace.ts:184`), `detectProjectProfile()` (`src/project/detector.ts:158` — returns `ProjectProfile` with `language` and `testFramework`; `detectTestFramework` is private and must **not** be imported), `detectLanguage()` (`src/project/detector.ts:125`, optional standalone use). Reuse `nax detect`'s test detection (Q2): `detectTestFilePatternsForWorkspace(workdir, packageDirs)` (`src/test-runners/detect/index.ts:199`) — the exact four-tier detector `nax detect` (`src/commands/detect.ts`) runs — produces the per-package `testFilePatterns` for `PackageFacts`. Do not call `resolveTestFilePatterns` directly or hand-roll detection.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a fixture with only a root `package.json` and a lockfile, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it returns a `RepoAnalysis` whose `shape` is `"single"` and whose `packages` array has length 1.
Given a fixture declaring `workspaces` with N member packages, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it returns `shape` equal to `"mono"` and a `packages` array of length N.
Given a fixture containing `bun.lock`, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it returns `pmRunPrefix` equal to `"bun run"` and `pmDlx` equal to `"bunx"`.
Given a fixture containing `package-lock.json`, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it returns `pmRunPrefix` equal to `"npm run"` and `pmDlx` equal to `"npx"`.

Given a package whose `package.json` scripts omit `type-check` and `lint:fix`, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then the matching `PackageFacts.missingScripts` array includes both `"type-check"` and `"lint:fix"`.
Given a root `turbo.json`, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it returns `orchestrator` equal to `"turbo"`.
Given a single-package fixture with no `turbo.json` or `nx.json`, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it returns `orchestrator` equal to `"none"`.

Given a package fixture using a Jest config, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then the matching `PackageFacts.testFramework` equals `"jest"` and `PackageFacts.testFilePatterns` comes from `detectTestFilePatternsForWorkspace`.
Given a member package at `packages/foo`, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then the matching `PackageFacts.relativeDir` equals `"packages/foo"` and is never an absolute path.
suggestedCriteria: Given a repo where `discoverWorkspacePackages()` returns an empty array, when `analyzeRepo` runs, then it still emits one root package entry rather than an empty `packages` list.
Given a package without `package.json`, when `analyzeRepo` inspects it, then it reports no executable scripts for that package and still preserves the package's `relativeDir` in the analysis output.

userStories.title: Generate and validate setup plans through the shared LLM path
acceptanceCriteria: Given a fenced ```json output and a `RepoAnalysis` input, when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then it returns a `SetupPlan` whose `config` is accepted by `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse`.

Given a plan whose `quality.commands.test` names a script absent from the `RepoAnalysis` input, when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then the returned `SetupPlan.config.quality.commands` excludes that command and the returned `gaps` array records it.

Given output that is not valid JSON (all `parseLLMJson` extraction tiers exhausted), when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then it throws `ParseValidationError` so the failure triggers the same-session retry path.
Given a schema-invalid `config`, when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then it throws `ParseValidationError`.
Given a `RepoAnalysis` with `shape` equal to `"single"`, when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then it returns a `SetupPlan` whose `monoConfigs` array is empty.
Given a `RepoAnalysis` with `shape` equal to `"mono"` and N packages, when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then it returns N `monoConfigs` entries.
When `setupGenerateOp.build(analysis)` runs, then it returns the string produced by `new SetupPromptBuilder().build(analysis)`.

Given an injected session that returns a schema-invalid config on every turn, when `callOp` is invoked with `setupGenerateOp`, then it rejects with a `NaxError` whose `code` equals `"SETUP_PLAN_INVALID"` after `MAX_SETUP_LLM_ATTEMPTS` attempts.

Given a stubbed `callOp`, when the rewired `callLLM` in `init-context.ts` is invoked, then it calls `callOp` with `setupGenerateOp` and resolves to that result instead of throwing `"callLLM not implemented"`.
suggestedCriteria: Given LLM output with extra narration around the JSON body, when `setupGenerateOp.parse` runs, then it still parses through `parseLLMJson()` and validates the extracted JSON payload.
Given a mono plan whose `monoConfigs` contain package dirs not present in `RepoAnalysis`, when `buildMonoConfigs` runs, then it excludes those entries from the returned `SetupPlan`.

userStories.title: Wire the setup command, config writes, reporting, and verification
acceptanceCriteria: Given an injected agent and a fixture directory, when `nax setup --dir <fixture>` runs, then it exits 0 and produces a `.nax/config.json` whose parsed content is accepted by `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse`.
Given a monorepo fixture, when `nax setup` runs, then it produces one `.nax/mono/<relativeDir>/config.json` per member package.
Given a single-package fixture, when `nax setup` runs, then it produces no `.nax/mono` directory.
When `nax setup --dry-run` runs, then it exits 0, creates no files under `.nax`, and prints the planned root config summary to stdout.
Given `generateSetupPlan` rejects with a `NaxError` whose `code` equals `"SETUP_PLAN_INVALID"`, when `nax setup` runs, then it exits 1 and writes no `.nax/config.json`.
Given a fixture that already has a `.nax/config.json` and no `--force`, when `setupCommand` runs, then it resolves without overwriting the existing file and exits non-zero.
Given a fixture that already has a `.nax/config.json`, when `setupCommand --force` runs, then it replaces that file's content with the generated config.
Given a `SetupPlan` carrying `gaps`, when `setupCommand` runs in report-only mode, then it emits each gap as a warning on stderr and exits 0.
Given a leaf package fixture and a stubbed gate runner, when `setupCommand` runs, then it invokes the configured verification gate exactly once.
Given a gate runner that reports a non-zero result, when `setupCommand` runs, then it exits non-zero.

Given a stubbed `analyzeRepo`, when `setupCommand` runs, then `analyzeRepo` is invoked once with the resolved workdir and `generateSetupPlan` is invoked with the `RepoAnalysis` that `analyzeRepo` returned.
Given the CLI registration in `bin/nax.ts`, when `nax setup` is invoked, then it dispatches to `setupCommand`.
suggestedCriteria: Given a `SetupPlan` whose root config has no surviving verification-capable command after cross-checking, when `setupCommand` runs, then it reports that no gate could be verified and exits non-zero without writing a misleading success summary.
Given a dry run on a monorepo plan, when `setupCommand` prints its summary, then it includes both the root config and the planned mono-config relative directories.

userStories.title: Add optional fill-scripts remediation for missing quality gates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement `--fill-scripts` so setup can optionally add missing `type-check` and related passthrough tasks/scripts before config write and verification.

**Motivation** — It defaults to report-only (writes `.nax/` files, prints a gap report), with `--fill-scripts` to optionally add missing `type-check`/`lint:fix` scripts.

**Approach** — It defaults to report-only (writes `.nax/` files, prints a gap report), with `--fill-scripts` to optionally add missing `type-check`/`lint:fix` scripts.

**Scope** — In: package.json script insertion, idempotent re-run behavior, root-vs-package handling, turbo task/root passthrough updates for monorepos, re-analysis seam to confirm missing scripts are cleared, and conditional invocation from `setupCommand`. Out: broader command synthesis beyond the explicitly supported missing gates.

**Interface**
```typescript
// Creates (per story)
// - src/cli/setup-fill.ts
```

**Notes** — `setupCommand` invokes `fillScripts` only when `--fill-scripts` is passed. The implementation should follow the repo’s immutable JSON-edit style used in adjacent CLI code and preserve existing scripts unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a `PackageFacts` missing `type-check`, when `fillScripts` runs, then it writes a `type-check` script equal to `"tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"` into that package's `package.json` and leaves existing scripts present and unchanged.
Given the same package, when `fillScripts` runs twice, then the resulting `package.json` has a single `type-check` key and the second run adds no duplicate entry.
Given `shape` equal to `"mono"` with a turbo orchestrator, when `fillScripts` runs, then it adds a `type-check` task to `turbo.json` and a `type-check` passthrough script to the root `package.json`.
Given `shape` equal to `"single"`, when `fillScripts` runs, then it adds the `type-check` script to the root `package.json` only and writes no orchestrator task.
Given a fixture where `fillScripts` has run for the filled gates, when `analyzeRepo` runs again over the same fixture, then the resulting `PackageFacts.missingScripts` no longer lists those gates.
Given `setupCommand --fill-scripts`, when `setupCommand` runs, then it invokes `fillScripts` before the write step.
Given `setupCommand` without `--fill-scripts`, when it runs, then it does not invoke `fillScripts`.
suggestedCriteria: Given a package that already defines `lint:fix`, when `fillScripts` runs, then it preserves the existing command text rather than replacing it with a generated value.
Given a monorepo root without `turbo.json`, when `fillScripts` runs, then it updates only package/root `package.json` files and does not create a new orchestrator manifest.

analysis:
This is an enhancement to an existing TypeScript/Bun CLI, not a greenfield feature. The new work needs to extend the current `init`/CLI/operation infrastructure instead of introducing parallel patterns. Existing CLI registration is centralized in `bin/nax.ts`; the `init` command is registered there with the lazy-import action style the spec wants mirrored, and the insertion point for `setup` is immediately after the `init` block at `bin/nax.ts:134-190`. The CLI barrel currently exports `initCommand` but nothing for setup, so `src/cli/index.ts:5-54` must be updated to export `setupCommand` and any option types. The existing `init` command already contains reusable collision behavior via `checkInitCollision()` at `src/cli/init.ts:64-84`, and the project-level init flow shows the repo convention for dependency injection and `.nax/` filesystem writes at `src/cli/init.ts:16-18` and `src/cli/init.ts:203-229`.

The most important existing gap is real and directly called out by the spec: `_initContextDeps.callLLM` is still a placeholder that throws `"callLLM not implemented"` at `src/cli/init-context.ts:44-49`, and AI context generation calls it from `src/cli/init-context.ts:286-312`. That means `nax init --ai` currently has a broken LLM path. There is also an interface risk here: today `callLLM` only accepts a `prompt: string`, but the spec requires rewiring it to `callOp(ctx, setupGenerateOp, ...)`, which implies either widening the helper contract or introducing a thin adapter so `init-context` can construct the `RepoAnalysis`-like input it needs without breaking current tests that stub `callLLM` by prompt alone. Existing tests already mock this seam in `test/unit/cli/init-context.test.ts:1-17` and via direct `_initContextDeps.callLLM` overrides found throughout that file, plus `test/unit/cli/init.test.ts:12-14`; these tests will need updates if the dependency signature changes.

The canonical LLM integration pattern is already present and should be reused, not reinvented. `planDraftOp` is the closest run-kind example: it declares `kind: "run"`, `session: { role: "plan-draft", lifetime: "fresh" }`, `noFallback: true`, a retry factory, a prompt builder, and a parse function at `src/operations/plan-draft.ts:165-181`. `callOp()` handles all dispatch, session lifecycle, retry handoff, and post-parse behavior, so `setupGenerateOp` should plug into that same contract rather than call adapters directly; the run-kind branch and session-role selection are handled in `src/operations/call.ts:123-145` and `src/operations/call.ts:232-260`. Operation exports are centralized in `src/operations/index.ts:1-117`, so the new op must be added there or downstream imports will fragment. JSON extraction for LLM outputs should use `parseLLMJson()` from `src/utils/llm-json.ts:111-164`, which already supports fenced ```json blocks and loose JSON recovery. Retry should use the existing parse-retry framework exported from `src/agents/retry/index.ts:1-9`; `makeParseRetryStrategy()` at `src/agents/retry/parse-retry.ts:43-117` is the shared parser-retry seam that works specifically with `ParseValidationError`.

Session roles are a hard SSOT. The new `setup` role must be added to the `CanonicalSessionRole` union and `KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES` list in `src/runtime/session-role.ts:9-53`, and the run-kind role table in `.claude/rules/adapter-wiring.md:39-46` must be kept in sync because the repo explicitly documents that `SessionManager.nameFor(req)` and adapter wiring consume that list as the source of truth. There is existing test coverage for role registration in `test/unit/runtime/session-role.test.ts` and precedent for adding a new role in tests like `test/unit/operations/plan-critic-llm.test.ts`, which already assert session-role registration for prior additions.

Repo analysis should reuse existing deterministic detectors exactly as the spec says. Stack/runtime/linter/monorepo heuristics already live in `detectStack()` and related helpers at `src/cli/init-detect.ts:69-230`; these are synchronous and currently produce heuristic quality commands, but `nax setup` should consume them as facts rather than reuse their command templates blindly. Workspace discovery already exists and is monorepo-aware in `discoverWorkspacePackages()` at `src/test-runners/detect/workspace.ts:152-189`; it returns relative paths, caches results per workdir, and is already used elsewhere in the codebase. Language and test framework detection belong to `detectProjectProfile()` at `src/project/detector.ts:158-174`, with `detectLanguage()` exported separately at `src/project/detector.ts:125-130`; the private `detectTestFramework()` is intentionally hidden, so implementations must not try to import it directly. Test-file pattern discovery for root and packages already has an exact workspace API in `detectTestFilePatternsForWorkspace()` at `src/test-runners/detect/index.ts:195-209`, which returns a map keyed by `""` for root and relative package dirs for members.

The closest writeback precedent for per-package config files is `nax detect --apply`. `detectCommand()` loads the root config, discovers packages, reads `.nax/mono/<dir>/config.json`, and writes raw JSON using helper functions at `src/commands/detect.ts:104-118` and `src/commands/detect.ts:137-260`. That is a strong model for `setup-write.ts`: root config goes to `.nax/config.json`, monorepo overrides go to `.nax/mono/<relativeDir>/config.json`, and package-relative paths stay relative. The spec also requires collision refusal when `.nax/config.json` already exists and `--force` is absent; `init` already enforces a similar overwrite guard in CLI flow at `bin/nax.ts:167-172`, and `checkInitCollision()` in `src/cli/init.ts:64-84` is the explicit collision pattern the spec says to mirror.

Config validation should go through `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse()` from `src/config/schemas.ts:36-220`. This schema already carries defaults for `quality.commands`, `execution`, and related nested config, so setup generation should validate the LLM-produced root config against the same runtime parser instead of inventing a separate schema. Existing schema-heavy tests already cover many config behaviors in files such as `test/unit/config/quality-commands-schema.test.ts`, `test/unit/config/schemas.test.ts`, and `test/unit/config/defaults-ssot.test.ts`, which reduces risk for schema-level regressions but increases the risk that setup writes configs with unintended defaults if raw object merging is sloppy.

Prompt builders are centralized behind the public barrel. `src/prompts/index.ts:1-73` explicitly says other subsystems should import prompt builders from the barrel rather than internal paths. Existing builder precedent lives in files like `src/prompts/builders/plan-builder.ts`, and the new `SetupPromptBuilder` must be exported from `src/prompts/index.ts` to satisfy the prompt-builder convention and avoid orphaned prompt code.

Current test coverage around adjacent systems is strong and should guide story design. `test/unit/cli/init.test.ts:1-80` covers filesystem writes and init scaffolding conventions. `test/unit/cli/init-context.test.ts:1-80` covers scan/template/LLM orchestration in init-context. `test/unit/test-runners/detect.test.ts:1-80` covers the four-tier test-pattern detection entrypoints and demonstrates the repo’s `_deps` mocking style. `test/unit/project/detector.test.ts:1-80` exercises `detectProjectProfile()`. `test/unit/operations/plan-draft.test.ts:1-90` verifies run-kind op identity, build behavior, parse validation, and retry seams. There is also workspace memoization coverage in `test/unit/test-runners/workspace-memo.test.ts` and session-role coverage in `test/unit/runtime/session-role.test.ts`. New `nax setup` tests should follow these patterns instead of introducing ad hoc test harnesses.

Primary impact areas are: CLI registration and barrels (`bin/nax.ts`, `src/cli/index.ts`); repo-analysis and type modules under `src/cli/`; LLM operation and prompt-builder plumbing (`src/operations`, `src/prompts`); init-context LLM rewiring (`src/cli/init-context.ts`); session-role SSOT (`src/runtime/session-role.ts`, `.claude/rules/adapter-wiring.md`); file writing and verification helpers; and optional script-filling logic that mutates `package.json` and orchestrator manifests. The highest-risk behavior changes are: 1) changing the `callLLM` seam used by existing init-context tests, 2) incorrectly mapping commands that do not exist and thereby writing broken quality gates, 3) misclassifying single-package vs monorepo repos due to mixed detector reuse, 4) writing absolute package paths into `.nax/mono` instead of relative dirs, and 5) mutating root/package scripts or `turbo.json` non-idempotently under `--fill-scripts`.

Backward compatibility expectations are mostly additive. `nax setup` is a new top-level command, and `nax init --ai` should start working by sharing the new LLM path instead of throwing. Existing repos that already have `.nax/config.json` must not be overwritten without `--force`, which is the migration guard. The migration path for users is straightforward: run `nax setup` in report-only mode to generate `.nax/config.json` and optional `.nax/mono/.../config.json`, inspect gap warnings, then rerun with `--fill-scripts` if they want the command layer normalized. There is no schema migration requirement beyond writing valid existing `NaxConfig` documents, but there is a config-behavior migration from heuristic `init` templates to verified commands that actually exist in package scripts/orchestrator tasks.
